name: fmt
algorithm: Format and parse back n signed 64-bit integers and n doubles with the language's std formatting and parsing (shortest round-trip digits for the doubles where the std has them); rounds times (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; formatting has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the checksum is taken over the parsed-back values (B18), never the output bytes, so it is the same whatever digits each std prints
notes: B18: C's std has no shortest round-trip float format, so the c cell prints %.17g (round-trips, but longer output than the other columns: not the same work); mk, rust, zig, go and cs (double.TryFormat "G") print the shortest round-trip digits.
Checksum: the wrapping sum of every parsed integer and of every parsed double truncated toward zero, plus the number of doubles that parsed back bit-exact (n per round when every format round-trips).
